Joint tests of each term across equations

Source: R/tests_fit.R
term_test.Rd

For every term of the model, tests that its coefficients are zero in all equations at once: the Wald form from the fitted covariance, or the likelihood-ratio form by refitting without the term (Stata's mlogtest, wald and lr). For a generic coefficient on an alternative-specific covariate the test has one degree of freedom. The terms are those of the outcome equations; for an inflated model the split-equation coefficients are not included (test them by lr_test() between two imnl() fits that differ in the split equation, or from the infl_ rows of summary.choicemodel()).

Usage

term_test(object, type = c("wald", "lr"))

Arguments

object

A fitted choice model.

type

"wald" (default) or "lr".

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per term: term, statistic, df, p.value.

Details

The likelihood-ratio form works as follows:

  • The model without the term is fitted as the estimators fit a model, multistart and saddle step included, so that both log-likelihoods are maxima; a warning says when that fit did not converge or still stops at a saddle.

  • For a maximum-likelihood fit of separated data (mnl(), rologit() without unit fixed effects or inflation), it compares the suprema of the log-likelihoods, not where the optimizer stopped (see lr_test()). The method line says so.

  • For a penalized fit (firth = TRUE or a prior), it is the penalized likelihood ratio: the term's coefficients are set to zero in the full model's penalized log-likelihood.

The Wald form of a penalized fit uses the penalized estimates and their covariance; for a separated coefficient it can be far off (see summary.choicemodel()).

The likelihood-ratio form assumes independent cases (a fit's cluster does not enter it); the Wald form uses the fit's covariance, cluster-robust when the fit has one.

See also

combine_test(), lr_test()

Other specification tests: captivity_test(), combine_test(), hl_test(), rank_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
term_test(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#> Joint tests of each term across equations (Wald) 
#>  term statistic df p.value
#>    x1   145.392  2  <2e-16
#>    x2   107.417  2  <2e-16
